notes: ACCESS: plain requests over HTTPS, no blocking whatsoever, exactly as the prior Home-Decor pass recorded (Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Sites-fv-Site). robots.txt names no anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web agent. TREE: taken from the homepage mega-menu (all category links are absolute origin URLs in the served HTML) and cross-checked against sitemap_index.xml -> sitemap_4-category.xml (753 category URLs), which surfaced nodes absent from the nav. QTY METHOD: the rendered listing header 'View N items' on each category page is the source of truth. Every leaf was read twice in separate passes and every number came back byte-identical (zero drift). On each page the site's Constructor.io attribute data-cnstrc-num-results carries the same integer as the header, and the Constructor browse API (ac.cnstrc.com/browse/group_id/<id>) returns the same total_num_results, so all three sources agree on all 33 leaves. Counts differ per category (no site-wide constant), none is suspiciously round, and every leaf URL is self-canonical with a breadcrumb matching the node loaded - the single exception is Office Storage, which serves no rel=canonical tag at all (flagged). HIERARCHY: the decisive test was product-ID containment, run by pulling full ID lists per node from the Constructor browse API. Under Sofas (975), Armchairs (416), Footstools (268), Dining Sets (642), Dining Tables (218) and Dining Chairs (496) every level-3 child proved to be a facet re-cut fully contained in its parent and heavily overlapping its siblings - e.g. Fabric sofas 546 + Leather sofas 402 = 948 against a 975 parent, and 2/3/4-seater + Corner = 955 of that same 975; Bar stools (75 of 75 IDs) and Dining benches (52 of 52 IDs) sit entirely inside Dining chairs; Corner sofas 205 of 205 and Sofa beds 44 of 44 sit entirely inside Sofas. Those level-3 nodes are therefore NOT emitted (they would double-count) and the level-2 product-type node is the leaf. Dropped on that basis: size cuts (2/3/4 seater, single / small double / double / king / super king, table and 4/6/8 chairs, 6 drawers, single/2-seater/3-seater/corner sofa beds), material cuts (fabric, leather, velvet, wooden, oak, ceramic, marble, glass, high gloss, metal, upholstered, mirrored), style/feature cuts (modern, traditional, chesterfield, rustic, industrial, cantilever, swivel, wingback, cuddle, tech, cinema, bi-fold / hinged / sliding / semi-fitted wardrobes) and price bands (sofas under 995/1495/1995, dining sets under 999/1399/1799, mattresses and bed frames under N). By contrast, under Living Room > Tables, Living Room > Storage, Living Room > Home Office, Bedroom > Furniture and Bedroom > Kids Furniture the children proved to be a genuine near-partition of the parent with little sibling overlap (Tables: children union 333 of the parent's 335 IDs; Storage 316 of 359; Home Office 95 of 104; Bedroom Furniture 982 of 1035; Kids Furniture 53 of 53), so those parents are grouping rows and their children are the leaves. Beds (326) is emitted as a grouping row rather than a leaf because it is a mixed roll-up: 40 of its 326 IDs are also in the Mattresses node and 47 of its product titles are mattresses, so only its furniture children are taken. EXCLUDED: Mattresses (189) and Kids mattresses (11) - bedding per brief; Bedding & pillows; the entire Accessories department (Lighting, Rugs, Wall Art, Mirrors, Home Furnishing), which is lighting / textile / wall decor / decor and was already covered by the Home-Decor pass. /dining-room/oak-furniture/ (325) and /bedroom/bedroom-furniture/oak-bedroom-furniture/ (100) are material cross-cuts that re-slice nodes already emitted (oak-furniture shares 50 IDs with Dining Tables and 59 with Living Room > Storage). /living-room/home-cinema-furniture/ (15) is a themed re-cut - 12 of its 15 IDs are already in TV Stands. /bedroom/bedroom-furniture/shelves/ (38) looks like a shelving category but 35 of its 38 IDs are already in Wardrobes and its tiles are wardrobes, so it is wardrobe shelving, not a shelving category; Living Room > Shelves (31) was checked by product title (Earth Ladder Shelving Unit, Riga Shelving Unit, Axis Shelving Unit, ...) and is genuine freestanding shelving furniture, so that one is kept. /bedroom/bedroom-furniture/wardrobes/wardrobe-interiors/ canonicalises back to Wardrobes and is furniture parts anyway. /dining-room/storage/* canonicalises to /living-room/storage/* (pure alias, kept once); the top-level slugs /sofas/, /armchairs/, /footstools/ and /upholstery/ all canonicalise to /sofas-and-armchairs/; /living/ canonicalises to /brands/. Per brief section 3: Sale / Clearance / Offers / Final reductions, Special buys, Best sellers, New, Quick delivery, Brands, Collections (Glamour, Scandi, Industrial, Modern, Rustic, Traditional, Mid-century), Inspire Me, Shop by room, /guest-room/ (9 items, a curated room edit) and TV ad. GARDEN FURNITURE: /garden-furniture/ plus its four children (garden-dining-sets, garden-sofas-and-lounge-sets, garden-accessories, garden-firepits-and-parasols) exist in the category sitemap, but all four children canonicalise to /garden-furniture/ and that page currently returns zero products (data-cnstrc-num-results=0, no 'View N items' header, page renders the empty-search template titled 'Your search for {0}'). Outdoor furniture is in scope but Furniture Village currently lists none, so no row is emitted rather than a zero or a guess. No bathroom-furniture and no nursery department exists anywhere on this site.
